title: Add miss-reason breakdown to cache miss metrics
author: Samir Qureshi
release_notes: - Runtime: KV/prefix cache miss counters now include a stable `reason` label (capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch). Dashboards/alerts can safely slice misses by reason without additional high-cardinality labels.
description: Summary: Extend KV cache + prefix cache miss telemetry to include a stable miss-reason taxonomy via a `reason` label on miss counters, and add validation notes/tests to ensure we don’t double-count in streaming/retry paths. Motivation: Hit-rate alone is insufficient to make the telemetry actionable; we need to answer “why did this miss happen?” to drive operator/customer recommendations (capacity sizing, TTL tuning, route policy, prompt canonicalization, rollout/version pinning). This PR implements the initial reason breakdown aligned with the ongoing cache telemetry sprint and SRE dashboard needs. Miss reasons added (stable taxonomy): - capacity: cache full / eviction pressure prevented reuse or insert - ttl_expired: entry existed but expired by TTL before reuse - policy_disabled: cache disabled by route/env/config (including per-route overrides) - hash_mismatch: canonicalization/hash does not match (prompt differences, tool-call serialization changes, etc.) - version_mismatch: model version (or compatible cache key version) mismatch during rollout / pinning change. Implementation details: - Introduces `CacheMissReason` enum and threads it through the existing miss accounting points for KV + prefix cache paths. - Emits `reason` label on miss counters only (NOT on histograms) to control series count and avoid ingestion blowups; this aligns with observability standards and the cardinality budget work. - Ensures reason attribution is mutually exclusive per miss event (single reason per miss) with a deterministic priority order when multiple conditions are true. Priority order implemented: policy_disabled > version_mismatch > ttl_expired > capacity > hash_mismatch. Rationale: policy/version/ttl/capacity are actionable “system states”; hash_mismatch is a catch-all for prompt/key divergence and is often noisy unless canonicalization is stabilized. - Adds explicit instrumentation comment blocks documenting when each reason is selected and what it means (so the taxonomy remains stable for dashboards/alerts). - Adds validation notes and tests for known tricky cases: streaming retries (avoid double counting), and continuous batching prefill paths (ensure miss is attributed to the request not the batch). Metrics: - `redwood_runtime_kv_cache_miss_total{cache="kv", reason="capacity|ttl_expired|policy_disabled|hash_mismatch|version_mismatch"}` - `redwood_runtime_prefix_cache_miss_total{cache="prefix", reason=...}` (same reason values). Note: naming aligns with the in-flight cache metric naming standardization; this PR intentionally only touches miss breakdown to reduce blast radius. Testing: - Unit tests for reason selection logic with table-driven cases. - Integration test updated to assert per-reason increments under controlled scenarios (policy off, TTL expiry, version pin change). - Local perf check: reason label adds no additional per-request allocations in the hot path (uses static string refs); counters remain sampled/guarded by existing telemetry flags. Rollout notes: - This is additive and safe to canary. Dashboards can start slicing by `reason` once ingestion rules allow the label. - Any downstream queries expecting a miss counter without `reason` must use `sum without (reason)` or be updated; existing dashboards in observability-pack are already moving to aggregations that tolerate new labels. Related: - ENG-4822 (implement hit/miss counters), ENG-4821 (define metrics/tags). - PR-18428 (fix metric double counting on stream retries) is a prerequisite for clean interpretation on streaming workloads; this PR includes assertions that should fail if that regression returns.

conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we confirm `reason` only lands on counters, not histograms? We can’t afford multiplying histogram series with another label. Also, please document the priority order—otherwise dashboards will become ambiguous when multiple conditions are true.
Samir Qureshi (author): Yep—only counters. Added explicit comment block + a unit test asserting priority and mutual exclusivity. Priority order now codified and documented in cache_metrics.rs.

Nadia Rahman (review): Please keep the taxonomy stable and align the strings with the standards doc (snake_case, no spaces). Also: I’m worried about `hash_mismatch` being used when the real issue is ‘not inserted due to capacity’. Ensure we don’t tag `hash_mismatch` for an insert failure that is actually eviction pressure.

Samir Qureshi (author): Updated logic so `capacity` covers both “no space to insert” and “evicted before reuse” signals; `hash_mismatch` is only used when we can compute a key and it does not match the stored key on lookup. Added tests for the insert-failure case.
Allison Grant (review): From SRE POV this is great. Request: add a note about how `version_mismatch` is expected during rollouts, so alerts should consider it separately (ticket not page).
Samir Qureshi (author): Added doc note + inline comment. We’ll mirror this in the dashboard spec (separate panel for version_mismatch).
Marcus Reed (review): Any perf risk from formatting reason strings on the hot path? Please avoid allocating Strings per request; use &'static str or an enum mapping table.

Samir Qureshi (author): Addressed—reason values are &'static str from a match; no heap allocation. Added a microbench note in the PR description and validated no measurable delta in our local perf smoke.
Noah Patel (review): One more: ensure we don’t double-count on streaming retries. I know PR-18428 was fixing it, but let’s add a regression assertion here if possible.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added integration assertion around retry path in the existing test harness; it fails if we emit multiple misses for the same logical request.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): LGTM after the priority order + no-histogram label changes. Please keep the taxonomy unchanged unless we ADR it.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved. Strings look aligned; telemetry schema impact is controlled.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Will start wiring panels to slice by reason once this lands in prod canary.
